newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'shita Elec eyes multimedia with 3DO technology.
newsitem.headline: M'shita Elec eyes multimedia with 3DO technology.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co will use interactive "M2" technology it acquired from 3DO Co to develop multimedia products for industrial and educational applications, a Matsushita spokesman said on Friday.
"The M2 will become the core technology for our future multimedia business, in fields such as educational products and digital TVs for industrial use," he said.
He added, however, that the company is not yet developing or planning any specific M2 products.
Matsushita on Thursday acquired full rights to use 3DO's M2 technology for interactive high-precision graphics processing, in exchange for returning 3.2 million 3DO shares to the U.S. company.

Matsushita in 1995 paid $100 million to 3DO to obtain exclusive rights to use the M2 technology, although 3DO had, until the deal announced on Thursday, retained the rights to sublicense M2 to hardware companies and software developers, as well as rights to royalty payments from Matsushita.
The M2 graphics processing technology has been touted as infusing cinema-quality sound and graphics to its applications, including game software.
Earlier this year, however, Matsushita announced it was withdrawing from the market for household game machines using the M2 technology, due to intensified competition.
